title: Canonical unbounded derived adjunction comparisons on arbitrary sheaf slices
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the chosen universe, with commutative coefficient rings and a structural map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $A$ be any sheaf of sets on the target, put $B=f^{-1}A$, and present the slices $\mathscr Y/A$ and $\mathscr X/B$ by the small element sites of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Write $R_{Y,A}$ and $R_{X,B}$ for the restricted rings and $r_Y,r_X$ for exact module restriction to these slices. There is a canonical ringed morphism $f_A:(\mathscr X/B,R_{X,B})\to(\mathscr Y/A,R_{Y,A})$ whose inverse image sends $(H\to A)$ to $(f^{-1}H\to B)$. Its ordinary module pullback and direct image satisfy $\sigma:f_A^*r_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Xf^*$ and $r_Yf_*\cong f_{A*}r_X$.
Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical K-flat pullbacks and K-injective direct images with their derived adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Exact restriction induces functors, denoted again by $r_X,r_Y$, on these derived categories. For every $M\in D(R_Y)$ and $E\in D(R_X)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$\theta_M:Lf_A^*r_YM\xrightarrow{\sim}r_XLf^*M,\qquad
\beta_E:r_YRf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{A*}r_XE.$$
Here $\theta$ is the canonical derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed slice square: on a K-flat complex $T$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] it is the image of $\sigma_T$ in the derived category, under the canonical representative identifications. Restriction of $T$ remains K-flat with flat terms. The map $\beta_E$ is represented, on a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], by the ordinary restriction/direct-image identity $r_Yf_*I\cong f_{A*}r_XI$; $r_XI$ is K-injective. Moreover $\beta$ is the adjunction exchange mate of $\theta$. In particular, for the canonical counits $\varepsilon$ of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $\varepsilon^A$ of $Lf_A^*\dashv Rf_{A*}$,
$$r_X(\varepsilon_E)\circ\theta_{Rf_*E}
=\varepsilon^A_{r_XE}\circ Lf_A^*(\beta_E).$$
No presentation of $f$ by a functor between the original sites, no flatness or invertibility of $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, and no boundedness assumption on the complexes is required.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; canonical square and module identities, extended to unbounded derived adjunctions by K-flat and K-injective representatives

proof.text: Obtain the normalized ordinary square, its module mates and the exact restriction functors from [lem-sbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-ordinary-comparison]. All derived structures are constructed from this ordinary output.

For either supplied module pullback, [lem-weil-pbc-supplied-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] gives a tensor pullback with the same right adjoint. Transfer preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes along the unique isomorphism of left adjoints. Flat-term K-flat resolutions give a resolving class on the homotopy category. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], then [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization], obtaining the derived adjunction and its chain-transpose formula on every complex, and invertible epsilon on flat-term K-flat complexes.

Exact restrictions give their derived functors and canonical representative factors. Apply the generic right-derived uniqueness comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-comparisons] to ordinary delta. Source restriction preserves K-injectives by the ordinary theorem, so both composites satisfy the right-derived universal property. This gives invertible beta and its representative equation on all complexes.

Define theta to be the inverse mate of beta. The ordinary mate equation, the normalized global derived unit, the equation for beta, and the local derived Hom normalization give the representative formula, using the generic mateOnRepresentative calculation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-mate-isIso].

For a flat-term K-flat resolution P, both epsilon comparisons are invertible; target restriction preserves the required flatness and K-flatness. The representative formula and invertibility of ordinary sigma show theta is invertible at QP. Naturality transports this along the resolution and the localization object-preimage isomorphism to every derived object. The mate bijection gives the mate equation, and its standard counit identity gives the required counit equation.

The statement is byte-identical to base, live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit and unreviewed. There is no repair note and the item is not in any dropped list. The only stmt_deps change adds def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, which the statement uses. Source: Stacks 04IF (sites-modules.tex line 2705) agrees with the ordinary square and f'_*j^*=j^*f_*. 04H1 gives the slice right adjoint G×_{f_*F}f_*E used in step 1. Tags 0G7E, 08FI, 07A6, 07A7, 08BJ, 070I, 09T5, 03EL, 03D7, 03D3, 06YY and 06YS all match their labels in tags/tags. No SGA is cited. Steps: (1) the slice right adjoint follows from the original adjunction, and L_A(F×A)=LF×B. (2) Restricting c gives the ring map. module-pullback-tensor is applied to j_B with ring O=f^{-1}R_Y and the identity map, so σ needs no flatness. (3) δ comes from V(E×B)=VE×VB. Its transpose identity uses geometric-module-transport, which says the module transpose is the underlying sheaf transpose. (4) right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective applies with v=j_! exact (stated in the slice-adjunction node), and kflat-pullback applies with c an isomorphism. (5) β is defined on a K-injective I. kinjective-hom-derived gives independence of the choice and naturality. (6) The direction of the inverse-mate formula matches def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate (G=r_Y, H=r_X). (7) h=(r_X i)σ_T termwise. (8) I checked the hypotheses of resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization. The normalization fixes the adjunction uniquely, and it is the 09T5 adjunction of projection-mate-exact. Pushing r_X(Q(i)ε_T) through by naturality gives θ_{QT}=Q(σ_T). (9) Invertibility follows by K-flat resolution, and the counit equation is exactly the transpose characterization of the mate. Duplicate search: every existing ringed-slice comparison node (derived-slice-localization, pullback-mate-normalization, slice-derived-comparisons, mate-isIso, comparisons-shift) assumes a continuous u and a site object V. The item strictly generalizes them and duplicates none. I accept all 12 declared tool_uses: they are generic module and derived tools, and sk-rem-rest is a stepless remark with no route. Edge cases checked: A terminal (identities), A empty (zero module categories), A representable (agrees with the site-object nodes), nonflat Z→Z/2 over a point. Two minor wording points need no change: R_{X,B}-linearity of σ in step 2, and in step 8 the reading of the canonical adjunction as the normalized one, which rests on 09T5 being their common origin. No fixes.
